idiom_name: sealed interface event hierarchy + kotlinx.serialization polymorphic form + SharedFlow
implementation_notes: A sealed interface with data-class cases is the event contract: the hierarchy is closed at compile time, so when exhaustiveness is compiler-checked, and it replaces the abstract event base class with compiler help instead of convention. kotlinx.serialization serialises the whole hierarchy with a class discriminator instead of a hand-written envelope plus type switch (subclassesOfSealed / polymorphic registration keeps it declarative), and delivery in-process is a MutableSharedFlow whose emit fans out to every collector - the flow replaces the publisher's subscriber list. For the wire form the same sealed hierarchy is serialised to JSON with the configured classDiscriminator, or mapped to a broker's own envelope.
pitfalls: kotlinx.serialization's default discriminator is the fully qualified class name; set an explicit @SerialName/classDiscriminator or moving a class silently breaks the wire contract.
SharedFlow's replay and buffer settings decide whether slow collectors lose events; with replay = 0 a collector that subscribes late sees nothing, and tryEmit drops when the buffer is full.
A sealed hierarchy cannot be extended from another module, which is exactly the exhaustiveness guarantee - do not defeat it by adding an open branch.
Collectors run until cancelled: launch them in a lifecycle scope (or a supervisor scope) or they leak with the enclosing component.
